What is the ZOTU Pipeline?

The ZOTU (Zero-radius Operational Taxonomic Unit) pipeline performs denoising on your amplicon sequencing data to identify true, exact biological sequences (also widely known as Amplicon Sequence Variants, or ASVs).

Unlike traditional 97% OTUs, ZOTUs are resolved down to 100% sequence identity. Sequences that differ by even a single nucleotide are kept separate as distinct biological variants, eliminating artificial clustering and preserving maximum biological resolution.

Below is an explanation of each output file in this folder and how to use it.

1Primary Abundance Tables

Table
ZOTUs-Table.tab
What it is
A tab-separated text table showing the exact number of times each ZOTU sequence was observed in each sample. Rows represent unique ZOTUs (ASVs), columns represent your samples, and the final column provides the assigned taxonomic classification (Domain down to Species).
Use it for
This is your high-resolution abundance table. Open it in Microsoft Excel, R, Python, or statistical software to analyze community structure, detect strain-level differences between groups, and perform differential abundance testing.
Table
SampleMinCount_Normalized-ZOTUs-Table.tab
What it is
A depth-normalized version of the ZOTU abundance table where all samples are subsampled (rarefied) to match the sequencing depth of the sample with the fewest reads.
Use it for
Fair, unbiased statistical comparisons of diversity (such as Shannon diversity or Bray-Curtis dissimilarity) without being distorted by differences in sequencing depth between samples.
Table
Spike_Normalized-ZOTUs-Table.tabPresent only if spike-ins were used
What it is
An abundance table normalized against the known concentration of internal DNA spike-in standards added to your samples.
Use it for
Absolute quantification. This allows you to estimate absolute microbial abundance (e.g., bacterial cells or copies per unit of sample) rather than relying only on relative percentages.

2Representative Sequences

Sequences
ZOTUs-Seqs.fasta
What it is
A standard FASTA file containing the exact, full-length DNA sequence for every identified ZOTU. Each sequence header includes the ZOTU identifier and its taxonomic assignment.
Use it for
Sequence-level investigations. You can use these sequences to query public databases (NCBI BLAST), align against specific reference genomes, construct phylogenetic trees, or design targeted primers.

3Phylogenetic Trees

Tree
ZOTUs-Tree-nj.tre
What it is
A phylogenetic tree of all ZOTU sequences in standard Newick format (.tre), built using the Neighbor-Joining method.
Use it for
Phylogeny-aware analyses, such as calculating weighted and unweighted UniFrac distances in QIIME 2, phyloseq, or R packages, and visualizing evolutionary relationships in tree viewers like FigTree or iTOL.

4Interactive Visualizations

Interactive
ZOTUs-Krona.html
What it is
An interactive, visual taxonomy chart (Krona plot) that opens in any web browser.
Use it for
Visually browsing the taxonomic composition of your ZOTUs. Double-click the file to open it in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge. Click through the concentric rings to easily explore proportions from Domain down to Species.

5SILVA 144+ Dual Outputs (*-8Levels.*)

Generated when a reference database with bacterial kingdoms is used, e.g. SILVA >= 144

Table
ZOTUs-Table-8Levels.tab
ZOTUs-Seqs-8Levels.fasta
ZOTUs-Krona-8Levels.html
SampleMinCount_Normalized-ZOTUs-Table-8Levels.tab
Spike_Normalized-ZOTUs-Table-8Levels.tabIf spike-ins were used
What they are
The exact same ZOTU results as above, but with 8 taxonomic ranks that include the bacterial Kingdom rank (e.g., Bacillati, Pseudomonadati, Fusobacteriati) between Domain and Phylum.
Use them for
Use the *-8Levels files if you need the latest SILVA 144+ kingdom classification. Use the standard (7-level) files above if downstream software (like PICRUSt2 or older R scripts) strictly requires classic 7-level taxonomies.
